kaps_punt: fossiele is die oorblyfsels van ou plante en diere wat in die rotse behoue gebly het; fossiele word gevind in lae van sedimentêre gesteentes; fossiele is bewyse van die geskiedenis van die lewe op aarde; daar is twee hoof tipes van fossiele, liggaam- en spoorfossiele

items.bewering: 'n Dooie dier vergaan gewoonlik heeltemal in die grond.
items.bron: NPS, How Fossils Form (home.nps.gov/subjects/fossils/how-fossils-form.htm); Open Access Government, 'How are fossils formed' (openaccessgovernment.org/article/how-are-fossils-formed/205905/): most remains are consumed by scavengers and decomposed by microbes and never preserved. 'Gewoonlik' is the right quantifier.

items.bewering: By 'n paar plante en diere van lank gelede bly daar tog iets agter. Die harde dele bly lê, of die vorm word in die sagte modder ingedruk.
items.bron: NPS, What is a Fossil? (nps.gov/subjects/fossils/what-is-a-fossil.htm): body fossils include bones, teeth, shells, and also molds, casts and impressions that record the shape of remains.

items.bewering: Die modder en sand daar rondom word oor 'n baie lang tyd hard. Wat so in die rots bewaar bly, noem ons 'n fossiel.
items.bron: USGS, Fossils, Rocks and Time: Rock Layers (pubs.usgs.gov/gip/fossils/rocks-layers.html): sediments bury organisms and harden into sedimentary rock, and the skeletons and plant pieces can become fossils. NPS, What is a Fossil?: fossils are evidence of life preserved in a geologic context, mainly in sedimentary rock.

items.bewering: Die meeste dooie plante en diere word nooit fossiele nie.
items.bron: NPS, How Fossils Form; Open Access Government, 'How are fossils formed': most dead organisms never fossilize because scavengers and decomposers remove them first. 'Die meeste' is accurate and not overstated.

items.bewering: Ander diere, insekte en piepklein lewende dinge eet 'n dooie lyf gewoonlik vinnig op.
items.bron: Open Access Government, 'How are fossils formed' (university-authored review): carnivores, scavengers and microbial agents (fungi and bacteria) are the main factors removing remains; soft tissue breaks down within days to weeks.

items.bewering: Wind en reën dra die res daarna stukkie vir stukkie weg. 'n Fossiel vorm daarom eers wanneer 'n paar dinge saam regloop.
items.bron: NPS, How Fossils Form; NPS Fossil Cycle Reading (nps.gov teacher lesson plan): burial soon after death protects remains from decay, weathering and scavenging; exposed remains are destroyed by weathering.

items.bewering: Modder of sand moet die plant of dier toemaak.
items.blok: Wat moet gebeur, en wat die kans beter maak
items.bron: USGS, Rock Layers; NPS, How Fossils Form: burial by sediment is the step that makes rock fossils possible. Exceptions (amber, ice, tar) lie outside the lesson's own definition of a fossil as something preserved in rock, so the 'moet' holds within the lesson.

items.bewering: Hoe gouer dit toegemaak word, hoe beter is die kans.
items.blok: Wat moet gebeur, en wat die kans beter maak
items.bron: NPS, How Fossils Form; Open Access Government, 'How are fossils formed': rapid burial reduces decay and scavenging and improves the odds of preservation.

items.bewering: Harde dele wat kan bly lê, maak die kans baie beter.
items.blok: Wat moet gebeur, en wat die kans beter maak
items.bron: NPS, How Fossils Form; Open Access Government, 'How are fossils formed': bones, teeth and shells are durable and survive better than soft tissue.

items.bewering: Alles moet dan 'n baie lang tyd so bly lê.
items.blok: Wat moet gebeur, en wat die kans beter maak
items.bron: USGS, Rock Layers: sediment must accumulate and harden into rock over geological time for the fossil to be preserved in it.

items.bewering: Fossiele lê byna altyd in sedimentêre gesteente
items.bron: NPS, What is a Fossil?: fossils are mainly found in sedimentary rock; 'more rarely' in volcanic rocks, and also in caves and soils. 'Byna altyd' matches; the lesson does not say 'altyd'.

items.bewering: hierdie rotse [sedimentêre gesteente] in lae bo-op mekaar vorm
items.bron: USGS, Rock Layers: 'Sedimentary rocks are formed particle by particle and bed by bed, and the layers are piled one on top of the other.'

items.bewering: Sandsteen en kalksteen is twee gesteentes wat uit sulke lae kom. Die lae van sandsteen was eens los sand.
items.bron: USGS, Rock Layers (sedimentary rock forms as particles accumulate and harden; its photographs show bedded limestone); Wikipedia, Limestone (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limestone): limestone is a sedimentary rock. Sandstone is lithified sand by definition.

items.bewering: Dit was juis daardie sand wat die plant of dier toegemaak het. Die laag word later hard, en die fossiel sit daarin vas.
items.bron: USGS, Rock Layers: sediment buries organisms and then hardens into rock with the fossil inside it.

items.bewering: Kalksteen lê ook in lae, maar dit vorm op 'n ander manier. Dit bestaan meestal uit die kalk van seediere se doppe en harde dele.
items.bron: Wikipedia, Limestone: most limestone grains are skeletal fragments of marine organisms; Earthlearningidea Virtual Rock Kit (earthlearningidea.com): fossiliferous limestone is shells and skeletons of sea creatures cemented by calcium carbonate; Hemel Hempstead Geological Society handout (hhgs.org.uk): skeletal fragments of brachiopods, crinoids, trilobites, corals. Some of the skeletal material comes from single-celled organisms and algae rather than animals, but 'meestal' and 'seediere' is a fair simplification at Grade 5 and does not mislead.

items.bewering: Sandsteen en kalksteen is twee rotse waarin mense fossiele kry.
items.bron: USGS, Rock Layers (fossil-rich limestone photographs); Earthlearningidea (fossiliferous limestone); NPS, What is a Fossil? (fossils in sedimentary rocks deposited in a variety of environments).

items.bewering: Waar 'n pad deur 'n heuwel gesny is, sien jy dikwels rotslae duidelik bo-op mekaar.
items.blok: Wat die lae vir ons sê
items.bron: USGS, Rock Layers: its Kentucky photograph shows horizontal limestone layers exposed where rock was removed to build an interstate highway.

items.bewering: Elke laag is bo-op die een neergesit wat reeds daar was. Die onderste laag was dus eerste daar en die boonste laag laaste.
items.blok: Wat die lae vir ons sê
items.bron: USGS, Rock Layers (Law of Superposition): 'a given bed must be older than any bed on top of it.' The 'eerste' and 'laaste' are stated for undisturbed layers and are qualified in the next sentences.

items.bewering: Waar die lae nog netjies op mekaar lê, is 'n fossiel laer af vroeër toegemaak as een hoër op.
items.blok: Wat die lae vir ons sê
items.bron: USGS, Rock Layers: superposition gives the relative ages of layers and of the fossils within them, in an undisturbed sequence.

items.bewering: Rotslae word egter soms later skeefgedruk of selfs heeltemal omgekeer.
items.blok: Wat die lae vir ons sê
items.bron: USGS, Rock Layers: layers that are no longer horizontal were tilted by later events such as mountain building. Wikipedia, Way up structure (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Way_up_structure) and Athabasca University Geology 319, Unit 2 (geol319r4.athabascau.ca/unit02.htm): beds can be overturned by later deformation, e.g. in recumbent folds and thrusting.

items.bewering: Waar lae omgekeer is, is die onderste laag nie meer die eerste een nie.
items.blok: Wat die lae vir ons sê
items.bron: Wikipedia, Way up structure; Athabasca University Geology 319, Unit 2: in overturned beds the younging direction is reversed, so the lowest bed is the youngest; geologists use way-up indicators to tell.

items.bewering: Een laag beteken ook nie een jaar nie. Een storm kan 'n hele laag in een dag neersit.
items.blok: Wat die lae vir ons sê
items.bron: Geological Digressions, 'Storm surges and tempestites' (geological-digressions.com/storm-surges-and-tempestites/); Copernicus Climate of the Past discussion supplement (cp.copernicus.org/preprints/9/C168/2013/): a storm lasting days can lay down a storm bed up to about 0.5 m; storm beds (tempestites) are deposited in hours to days. 'Kan' is the right modal; the lesson does not say every layer forms this fast.

items.bewering: Tog bewaar die rotse vir ons 'n rekord van daardie lewe.
items.bron: NPS, What is a Fossil?: fossils 'provide the history of life on Earth'; 'fossil record' is the standard term. Mapping checked: a learner might take 'rekord' as complete, but the block 'Dit gebeur selde' already says most living things never become fossils, so the comparison does not imply a complete record.

items.bewering: Elke fossiel is 'n stukkie bewys dat so 'n plant of dier werklik bestaan het.
items.bron: NPS, What is a Fossil?: a fossil is by definition the remains, traces or imprints of a past living organism, i.e. evidence of life. Holds for trace fossils too, which prove an organism existed even when its maker is not identified.

items.bewering: Mense kan aan baie fossiele sien hoe groot 'n dier was en hoe hy gelyk het.
items.bron: NPS, What is a Fossil?: body fossils are better at showing an organism's anatomy. 'Baie' rather than 'alle' is correct.

items.bewering: Party van daardie plante en diere lewe nie meer op aarde nie. Ons ken hulle vandag uit die fossiele wat hulle agtergelaat het.
items.bron: NPS, What is a Fossil?: the fossil record helps us understand evolution and extinction. 'Party' understates the share (most species that ever lived are extinct) but is not false.

items.bewering: Fossiele word in twee hooftipes verdeel, en albei lê in dieselfde soort rots.
items.bron: NPS, What is a Fossil? (body fossils and trace fossils as the two categories); NPS Denali, Trace Fossils (home.nps.gov/dena/learn/nature/trace-fossils.htm): trace fossils are preserved in sedimentary rock, as body fossils are.

items.bewering: 'n Fossiel van 'n deel van 'n plant of dier se lyf is 'n liggaamfossiel.
items.bron: NPS, What is a Fossil?: body fossils are the remains of past animals, plants and microorganisms (bones, teeth, skin, shells, wood, leaves), including molds and casts of them.

items.bewering: 'n Spoorfossiel is 'n fossiel van 'n teken wat 'n plant of dier agtergelaat het, nie van 'n deel van sy lyf nie.
items.bron: NPS, What is a Fossil? and NPS Denali, Trace Fossils: trace fossils are evidence of an organism's activity, not its body (footprints, burrows, trails, coprolites, root traces). Root traces show that plants leave trace fossils too, so 'plant of dier' is correct.

items.bewering: fossiel: Iets wat 'n plant of dier van lank gelede in rots agtergelaat het.
items.bron: NPS, What is a Fossil?: the remains, traces or imprints of past living organisms preserved in a geologic context, mainly sedimentary rock. Read on its own, the entry is true and covers both body and trace fossils.

items.bewering: liggaamfossiel: 'n Fossiel van 'n deel van 'n plant of dier se lyf.
items.bron: NPS, What is a Fossil?: body fossils are the remains of past organisms.

items.bewering: spoorfossiel: 'n Fossiel van 'n teken wat 'n plant of dier agtergelaat het, nie van 'n deel van sy lyf nie.
items.bron: NPS, What is a Fossil?; NPS Denali, Trace Fossils: evidence of activity (prints, burrows, coprolites, root traces) without any part of the organism.

opsomming: All 32 checkable claims, including three sequence superlatives (eerste/laaste), the 'die meeste' quantifier and the 'rekord' comparison, check out against USGS, NPS and geology sources; the quantifiers (gewoonlik, byna altyd, meestal, baie, kan) are already set at the right strength, so there is nothing to fix.
